Hello,
Thanks for reporting this, 0.12.0 should be available in maven, can you share the exact error you are having.
`iosX64` target is removed in 0.12.0, if you are using that target you will have an issue updating to 0.12.0, can you double check you no longer need it and it's removed from the latest versions of Kotlin and Compose.

Thanks for the quick reply! 
 
 You were right, the problem was on our side. We had iosX64() in all our KMP modules, that's why 0.12.0 couldn't resolve. After removing iosX64() from every module (kept only
 iosArm64() and iosSimulatorArm64()), 0.12.0 works fine now. 
 
 For anyone else running into this: if you're on an Apple Silicon Mac and don't need the Intel simulator, just remove iosX64() from your build.gradle.kts files. Simulator still 
 works via iosSimulatorArm64, real devices via iosArm64. 
 
 Closing this. Thanks for the library!

`calf-io` now has `suspend fun KmpFile.source(): kotlinx.io.RawSource`

Opening is blocking on Android/iOS/Desktop, so call it from `Dispatchers.IO`.

I went with kotlinx-io instead of a separate okio module: calf-io already depends on it. For your zip case the official bridge does the conversion:

```kotlin
implementation("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-io-okio:0.9.1")

import com.mohamedrejeb.calf.io.source
import kotlinx.io.okio.asOkioSource

val zip = ZipInputStream(file.source().asOkioSource().buffer())
```

This also removes the need for the canImportFile platform check, the same code now works everywhere.

On isFile: I left it as "not a directory". On Android every picked item is a content URI, so returning false would just make it always false there. The actual problem was that getPath() is not something you can open on Android, and source() is the answer to that. If you still need a "is this a real file system path" check after trying source(), let me know and we can add one.

Docs: https://mohamedrejeb.github.io/Calf/filepicker/#streaming-with-kotlinx-io
